_about: English definitions for the sample paper's glossary. Each language file gives the translations. Order here is the order of the glossary.

terms.language model: A model trained to predict text; the basis of chat assistants.
terms.next-token prediction: Training a model to guess the next word piece from the ones before it.
terms.hallucination: A fluent but false or unsupported statement produced by a model.
terms.retrieval-augmented generation: Generating an answer while conditioning on passages fetched from a document collection.
terms.retriever: The component that searches a collection for relevant passages.
terms.dense retriever: A retriever that compares questions and passages as vectors.
terms.cross-encoder: A model that reads a question and a passage together to score how well they match.
terms.passage: A short chunk of text from a document.
terms.inner product: The sum of element-wise products of two vectors, used as a similarity score.
terms.question answering: The task of answering questions written in natural language.
terms.benchmark: A standard dataset used to compare methods.
terms.exact-match accuracy: The share of answers that are identical to the reference answer.
terms.re-ranking: Reordering a list of candidates with a slower but more accurate model.
terms.generator: The model that writes the final answer.
terms.prompt: The text given to a language model as its input.
terms.learning rate schedule: How the size of training steps changes during training.
terms.cosine decay: Lowering the learning rate along a cosine curve.
terms.ablation: An experiment that removes one part of a system to measure its effect.
terms.parameter: A number inside a model that is learned during training.
terms.baseline: The reference method that a new method is compared with.
terms.inference: Using a trained model to produce outputs.
